description: railML is an open XML-based railway markup language for exchanging data between railway applications, defined by XSD schemas with subschemas for infrastructure, interlocking, rolling stock and timetable, each maintained by a working group, plus an ontology, documentation wikis, example data and the railVIVID viewer and validator. The railML.org initiative was founded in 2002 by Fraunhofer IVI Dresden and ETH Zurich and is run by the non-profit railML.org e.V. with partners including infrastructure managers and software vendors; railML 2.5 was adopted in 2022 as ISO/TS 4398 (RailDax), and railML 3 is based on the RailTopoModel. As a format it has no spatial coverage and is used to describe networks worldwide at the level of tracks, switches, signals and timetabled trains. Supported versions are 2.5 (September 2021) and 3.3 (November 2024), with 3.4 announced for November 2026. Schemas, example data and railVIVID are free after registration and acceptance of licence terms: version 3 schemas under a restricted CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence, version 2 under CC BY-NC-ND 3.0. Caveats: the non-commercial and no-derivatives terms restrict redistribution of modified schemas, and implementations differ in which subschemas they support. railML is the input and output format of many railway capacity planning, timetabling and network flow simulation tools and relates to the EU Register of Infrastructure (RINF) catalogued here.
